Author: topstockalerts
Text: Citigroup lines up Wall Street banks for Banamex IPO Citigroup is assembling major Wall Street banks for an IPO of Mexico’s Grupo Financiero Banamex that could raise more than $3 billion, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Citigroup is expected to lead the offering, with Bank of America, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase also involved. The banks are targeting January for the listing. Citigroup and Banamex are still assessing how much of Citi’s remaining stake could be sold before the IPO, with smaller stake sales possible. The plans remain under discussion and could change, while additional banks may join the syndicate. The IPO is part of CEO Jane Fraser’s broader retreat from consumer banking in international markets. Citi sold 25% of Banamex to Mexican billionaire Fernando Chico Pardo last year and another 24% to investors including General Atlantic and Blackstone, leaving it with about 51%. $C $BAC $GS $JPM

Author: topstockalerts
Text: JPMorgan Says Stocks Can Keep Rising Despite Higher Bond Yields JPMorgan’s Grace Peters said equities can continue advancing even as rising bond yields raise the hurdle for earnings growth. She pointed to solid economic growth, heavy bond supply needed to finance AI infrastructure and inflation concerns linked to oil prices above $100 a barrel as key drivers of higher yields. Peters said fixed income still has a role in portfolios but requires selectivity, while she favors equities as she expects an increasingly broad “earnings supercycle” to support portfolio growth. She said investors have already absorbed much of the recent increase in yields. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield has moved roughly 40 basis points this month, while a selloff in government bonds on Thursday pushed longer-term U.S. yields to their highest levels in more than two decades. The 10-year yield reached levels not seen since July 2007, with European yields also moving higher. $JPM

Text: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has hired three senior bankers to strengthen its natural-resources investment banking team, according to a memo reviewed by Bloomberg News. David Casson joins as head of North American mining investment banking in Toronto from Morgan Stanley, where he served as managing director of metals and mining for North America. Christopher Dahan joins as a managing director focused on natural-resources M&A in Houston, moving from Perella Weinberg’s TPH & Co., where he advised on energy and infrastructure transactions. Greg Kantrowitz joins as a managing director covering power, renewables and clean technology in New York. He previously led clean-energy transition coverage at Citigroup.
